heap-buffer-overflow.definition: A heap allocation can provide less capacity than writes performed through the returned region on a feasible path in this function.
positive_evidence: Relate an allocation-size expression to the maximum bytes subsequently written.
Account for terminators, separators, loop counts, element widths, and pointer increments.
Allow an allocation-like opaque call only when its argument and returned-pointer use make that role locally plausible; lower confidence accordingly.
exclusions: Do not flag an unsafe-looking copy without a locally supportable destination-capacity mismatch.
Do not count stack-only overflow or out-of-bounds read as this class.
Do not assume an opaque callee allocates a particular size beyond the displayed argument.

use-after-free.definition: A feasible path in this function releases an object while an alias remains live and later reads, writes, dereferences, or passes that stale reference.
positive_evidence: Identify the release operation, the surviving alias, and the later use.
Track aliases through assignments, container fields, and pool-slot reuse when locally visible.
exclusions: Allocation or pool reuse alone is insufficient without a locally visible stale use.
Do not invent freeing behavior for opaque callees.
Use indeterminate when the required free/use sequence necessarily lies outside the supplied function.

integer-overflow.definition: Bounded-width integer arithmetic can wrap or overflow on a feasible path and the corrupted value affects a security-relevant size, index, allocation, loop bound, pointer offset, or protection check in this function.
positive_evidence: Establish a plausible operand range and the relevant signedness or width despite decompiler uncertainty.
Connect the overflow to a consequential local operation or to bypass of a local check.
Consider checks whose own addition, multiplication, or cast can overflow.
exclusions: Arithmetic that can wrap but has no security-relevant local consequence is insufficient.
Do not treat every cast or unsigned wrap as a vulnerability.
State decompiler signedness uncertainty through confidence or indeterminate rather than silently assuming source types.

null-pointer-dereference.definition: A pointer can be NULL on a feasible path and this function dereferences it, performs pointer arithmetic requiring validity, or passes it to a locally recognized non-NULL-requiring operation before a sufficient guard.
positive_evidence: Trace the pointer from a nullable local source or branch to the first unsafe use.
Account for short-circuit conditions and guards on every relevant path.
Treat standard C library operations such as strchr or strlen as requiring a valid pointer.
exclusions: Do not assume every opaque call can return NULL unless local control flow supports that interpretation.
Do not flag a NULL value that is guarded before all dereferences.
Do not use caller preconditions that are not displayed.

out-of-bounds-read.definition: A feasible path computes a pointer or index outside a locally inferable readable object and then reads from that location in this function.
positive_evidence: Connect a bound, object extent, or ring-buffer extent to the final index used by a read.
Re-evaluate bounds after every index adjustment, wraparound correction, cast, or subtraction.
Identify the actual read expression and the path reaching it.
exclusions: Distinguish reads from writes and from arithmetic that never accesses memory.
Do not assume an object size solely from a decompiler-generated variable name.
Do not flag a path that exits before the read.

command-injection.definition: A string influenced by a function parameter or locally read input is incorporated into a command interpreted by a shell-capable sink in this function without adequate argument separation or validation.
positive_evidence: Show local data flow from the input-like value through command construction to a recognized sink such as system, popen, or an explicit shell invocation.
Assess allowlists, metacharacter rejection, quoting, and fixed argument-vector execution when they are locally visible.
Classify the dangerous local pattern without claiming external reachability or attacker control.
exclusions: String formatting alone is not command injection without a shell-capable sink.
Do not assume an opaque FUN_* callee invokes a shell without local evidence.
A fixed command with no parameter-derived content is insufficient.
